newsitem.title: UK: Tarabetic news wipes 24 pct off Scotia value.
newsitem.headline: Tarabetic news wipes 24 pct off Scotia value.

text.p: Nearly 24 percent of Scotia Holdings Plc's market value was wiped off by news the fledgling biotech firm would at present not receive approval to market its diabetic drug Tarabetic in Britain.
Shares in Scotia fell 135 pence to 435, after Scotia said the Medicines Control Agency could not recommend Tarabetic after a meeting with an advisory body which looks into the safety of new drugs.
Analysts said the news was a severe setback but noted the MCA decision is not final and Tarabetic is not the most important drug in Scotia's pipeline.
The MCA several times before has given the final go-ahead to drugs after initial negative advices from advisory bodies, analysts pointed out.
Some said the current slump in Scotia's shares offered a good buying opportunity.
"If ever there was a good time to buy biotech companies, then it was when they had setback," said Nick Woolf at Nomura.
He forecast Tarabetic would eventually grab sales of up to 120 million stg per year. Woolf expected annual sales for Scotia's cancer drug Foscan of about 280 million stg.
An update on Foscan's development is expected on March 25 when Scotia is scheduled to release its 1996 results.
